name: Paraguay
summary_text: Paraguay demands real caution from trans visitors — South America's most conservative country. There is no legal gender recognition (ten lawsuits on trans name recognition remain pending, unresolved), no anti-discrimination law covering gender identity, and no hate-crime statute. AP documents that many LGBTQ+ Paraguayans feel compelled to leave their hometowns due to discrimination, harassment, and gender-based violence; trans women face particular social rejection. Amnesty reports persistent structural discrimination and high gender-based violence. Nothing criminalises being trans, Asunción has a small organised community, and there is no documented police targeting pattern — the risk is social hostility and a total protection vacuum rather than state persecution. Tourist traffic is low and there are no documented trans-visitor incidents.

sources.claim_summary: AP (Sep 2025): 'For Paraguay's transgender women, survival often means leaving home' — discrimination, harassment and gender-based violence push trans women out of hometowns into migration and sex work.

sources.title: Human rights in Paraguay Amnesty International
sources.claim_summary: Amnesty International Paraguay report 2025: criminalization of human rights defenders and structural discrimination persisted; high levels of gender-based violence; threats against journalists and repression of social protest.

sources.title: Amnesty International (Author): “The State of the World's Human Rights; Paraguay 2024”, Document #2124661 - ecoi.net
sources.claim_summary: Amnesty International, State of the World's Human Rights - Paraguay 2024: rulings on 10 lawsuits regarding legal recognition of transgender people's names were still pending; a new bill and parliamentary commission of inquiry threatened civil-society freedom of association and expression; gender-based violence a huge concern.

sources.title: Paraguay will 'burn books' which don't promote 'traditional gender ideology' | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (Oct 2017): Paraguay's Ministry of Education banned public schools from using materials on 'gender ideology'; Education Minister Enrique Riera said he would 'burn books' spreading it; LGBT organisations called 'gender ideology' a phrase 'invented by conservative groups to keep justifying violence and discrimination'; Amnesty also condemned the move.

sources.title: Inter-American Court endorses same-sex marriage; Costa Rica reacts
sources.claim_summary: Tico Times (Jan 2018): the Inter-American Court of Human Rights ruled that all signatory countries must allow same-sex marriage - binding for most Latin American states including Paraguay; ~300 Costa Ricans celebrated at the court.

sources.title: Gays pueden adoptar niños - Notas - ABC Color
sources.claim_summary: ABC Color (in Spanish): 'Gays pueden adoptar niños' - Paraguayan media coverage of gay adoption (page largely navigation content at fetch time).

sources.title: Matrimonio igualitario: Sugieren adecuar leyes - Última Hora | Noticias de Paraguay y el mundo, las 24 horas. Noticias nacionales e internacionales, deportes, política. Noticias de
sources.claim_summary: Última Hora (Jan 2018, in Spanish): international human-rights expert Claudio Nash said Paraguay must adapt its laws for equal marriage per the IACHR recommendation - the Inter-American Court could oblige Paraguay to change its norms, and the country should start discussing implementation rather than wait for a judgment.
